_comment: Shared task board for Claude and Codex. Since 2026-09-02 the user's standing rule is that ALL coding is requested from Codex: Claude writes the spec here and reviews the diff. 'files' is the allowlist the diff is checked against - and when a task edits a GENERATOR, its committed OUTPUT belongs in that list too, or verifying the change reads as going out of bounds. Run one with: python -m company.orchestrator.main team run --task <id>

tasks.title: Casual/Korean UI layout in SceneGenerator
tasks.goal: Rebuild the title, HUD, game-over, pause and shop screens in SceneGenerator to match the approved casual direction: cream cards with a thick brown outline, Korean labels, one primary green button per screen.
acceptance: Every on-screen string is Korean.
The HUD shows distance and an in-run coin count.
Text is legible on a device - the built-in Latin-only font is not used for Hangul.
notes: Design reference: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/2c13a317-896d-45cc-98da-b01955e1bc92

tasks.title: Split distance from coins in the economy
tasks.goal: Score was the coin count and there was no distance metric at all. Score is now distance in metres (RunnerDistanceTracker), coins are the shop currency, and game over pays out coins rather than score.
acceptance: Currency earned per run is unchanged: one coin picked up is still one currency.
A run that collects nothing still scores, because distance accrues.

tasks.title: Map the four Kenney button colours
tasks.goal: The UI only has one button sprite (blue). The casual design needs green for the primary action, yellow for the shop, red for close and grey for secondary/disabled. Add the four colour variants from the already-approved kenney-ui-pack to the art mapping, and give each one its 9-slice border in SharedArtImporter so the outline keeps its thickness at any button size.
acceptance: art-mapping.json gains four targets: Assets/Common/Art/UI/button_green.png, button_yellow.png, button_red.png, button_grey.png.

Each uses packId kenney-ui-pack, archiveName kenney_ui-pack.zip, and sourceFile PNG/<Colour>/Default/button_rectangle_depth_flat.png with Colour one of Green, Yellow, Red, Grey - these exact paths are confirmed present in AI_GAME_COMPANY/asset_staging/kenney_ui-pack/INVENTORY.txt.
Each target has a 'why' field explaining the colour's role, matching the style of the entries already in the file.

SharedArtImporter.UiBorders gains an entry per file with the border new Vector4(4f, 8f, 4f, 4f) - the same measurement as the existing 'button' entry, because these are the same 192x64 sprite in a different palette.
The existing 'button' entry and the blue target are left alone.
The JSON stays valid and keeps its two-space indentation.
notes: Unity's spriteBorder order is (left, bottom, right, top) - that is why the bottom is 8 and not the top: the depth lip is at the bottom of the sprite.
Do not copy any image files. apply-art-mapping.ps1 does the copying on the PC, and it refuses any pack that is not APPROVED in LICENSE_REGISTRY.json.

Ran 2026-09-02. Codex edited both allowlisted files correctly; the run was reported BLOCKED only because Unity rewrote Packages/packages-lock.json while it worked - see CODEX-BOARD1 defect 1. Committed by hand as 89514dc. Still needs apply-art-mapping.ps1 -Commit to copy the actual PNGs, and a build to compile SharedArtImporter.

tasks.title: PlayMode tests for the distance/coin split
tasks.goal: GameManager just grew a second currency-like counter and a monotonic SetScore. The existing PlayMode tests only cover AddScore. Add tests that pin the new behaviour so a later refactor cannot quietly put distance back into the currency payout.
acceptance: A test proves SetScore ignores a value lower than or equal to the current Score.
A test proves AddCoins raises Coins and fires CoinsChanged, and is ignored once the state is GameOver.
A test proves StartGame resets both Score and Coins to zero.
A test proves TriggerGameOver adds Coins - not Score - to the saved currency, reading it back through SaveSystem.GetInt(gameId, ShopKeys.Currency).
A test proves IsNewBest and PreviousBest describe the record as it stood BEFORE the run ended.
Existing tests in the file still pass unchanged.
notes: Read Assets/GameFactory/Core/GameManager.cs and Assets/GameFactory/Core/SaveSystem.cs first - the API is new and is not what the older tests assume.
SaveSystem writes to PlayerPrefs, which persists between tests. Use a game id unique to each test, or clear the keys in SetUp, or the currency assertions will pass once and then drift.
Follow the arrange/act/assert shape and the [UnityTest] IEnumerator style already used in the file.

tasks.title: Give the character arms and legs that move
tasks.goal: The character is one sprite with squash/stretch and a bob. The user asked whether the arms and legs move - they do not. Add procedural limbs that run while grounded and hold a pose in the air, driven from the existing RunnerCharacterMotion so no new Update loop is introduced.
acceptance: Limbs are child GameObjects created at runtime by this component - do NOT change PrefabGenerator, and do not require any new art file.
They swing in opposite phase (left arm with right leg) at a rate tied to the same cycle the existing bob uses, so the gait reads as one motion.
In the air they stop cycling and hold a jump pose, and they return to the run cycle on landing.
The limbs are drawn BEHIND the body sprite, and they never affect the collider - the collider is on the root and this component only touches the Visual child.
No allocation per frame: create the limb objects once, then only set transform values in Update.
notes: Read the whole of RunnerCharacterMotion.cs first. It already tracks grounded state and vertical velocity from RunnerPlayerController, and it already compensates the foot position when the sprite squashes - reuse those, do not recompute them.
Sorting: a SpriteRenderer child needs a lower sortingOrder than the body to draw behind it.
Keep it subtle. This is a 136x192 sprite on a phone; limbs that swing far read as broken, not lively.

tasks.title: Gemini design adapter (free tier only, never escalates)
tasks.goal: Add company/orchestrator/gemini_client.py so design work can be requested from Gemini's free tier. Model it on the two adapters already in this repo - ollama_client.py and codex_runner.py - which enforce their cost rules in code rather than in prose. Text prompts return text; image prompts return PNG bytes the caller writes under AI_GAME_COMPANY/generated/.
acceptance: Reads the API key ONLY from the env var named by policy gemini_api_key_env (GEMINI_API_KEY). Never from GOOGLE_API_KEY, which stays on blocked_env_keys, and never from a file in the repo.

The key value is never logged, printed, put in an exception message, or written to disk. A status helper may report that a key is PRESENT or ABSENT and nothing more - copy the 'names only' idiom from CodexRunner.stripped_keys.
Raises a PolicyViolation (from company.orchestrator.policy) before any network call when policy allow_gemini_design is not true. Test that no request is attempted in that case.
Refuses any model id that is not in the policy's gemini_free_tier_models list, with its own exception type. This is the free-tier gate and it must be checked before the request, not after.

On HTTP 429 or a quota/rate-limit response, raises a GeminiLimited exception - the same 'degrade, never spend' shape as CodexLimited. It must NOT retry against another model, another tier, or a billed project.

An HTTP error, an empty response, or a response that is not the expected content type raises rather than returning something falsy. A generation that did not happen is never reported as a generation that produced nothing.
Uses only the Python standard library (urllib.request). Do not add a dependency - google-generativeai is not installed and must not be added.
Network calls are injectable so the tests need no key and no network: follow the 'runner' test seam CodexRunner uses.
Tests cover: the policy gate, the free-model gate, key absence, a 429 degrading, a malformed response raising, and that the key never appears in any exception text or status string.
notes: Endpoint shape, verified from this container on 2026-09-02: GET https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models returns 403 PERMISSION_DENIED with 'Please use API Key' when unauthenticated - so the host is reachable and only the key is missing. Use that same host.

Google's own pricing/rate-limit page (ai.google.dev) is BLOCKED by this environment's egress proxy, so the free tier could not be confirmed from a first-party source. Do not write a comment claiming specific free quotas. Write the code so that exceeding quota fails loudly instead.
Do NOT call the API during the tests. There is no key here and a test that needs one is a test that never runs.
Login/key setup is a HUMAN_GATE (initial_gemini_login in company_policy.json). Report it, never perform it.

tasks.title: Department office view on the dashboard
tasks.goal: Add one section to the dashboard that draws the connected AI as characters sitting in company departments, where each character's movement encodes that AI's real status. docs/OFFICE_VIEW_SPEC.md is the specification - read it first and follow it; it fixes the department mapping, the status-to-behaviour table and the constraints.
acceptance: docs/OFFICE_VIEW_SPEC.md is followed: the department mapping table, the four status behaviours, the floorplan layout with 외주 outside the building, and the 'do not' list at the end.

Adds a Gemini row to the agent roster in build_agents, so the design department is not drawn empty: state READY only if a key is present in the env var named by policy gemini_api_key_env, otherwise GATED naming initial_gemini_login as the gate, and BLOCKED if policy allow_gemini_design is not true. Evidence is config/company_policy.json. Report only whether a key is present - never its value.
Reads only the existing Snapshot.agents - no new file is parsed and no new data source is added.
An agent whose name matches no prefix in the mapping lands in a 기타 department rather than being dropped from the page.
Animation is CSS keyframes only. No JavaScript animation loop and no external library.
Every colour comes from an existing --token. No new colour is introduced, and no colour is defined only inside a @media or [data-theme] block.
Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce all movement stops, and status is still readable from colour and posture alone.
The section renders in the static file too (it is display-only, unlike the control panel), and produces no horizontal page scroll at 360px wide.
Each character carries a title/aria-label of its name and status, and links to the matching roster row.
A test asserts every state in dash.STATE_LABEL has a distinct visual class in the office CSS - if two statuses render identically the section is decoration, not information.
A test asserts an unmapped agent name still appears in the rendered HTML.

Regenerate Reports/dashboard.html with `python -m company.orchestrator.main dashboard` and leave the result in the working tree. That regenerated file is the only proof the section renders at all, since there is no other way to see it from here.
notes: Read dashboard.py fully first. It already has: the four status constants (READY/GATED/BLOCKED/UNKNOWN), the token palette in CSS, the e() escaping helper, and the section markup pattern. Reuse them.
Characters are procedural inline SVG. Do NOT add image files or any new licensed asset - v1 must work with zero assets. Keep the character drawing in one function so real art can replace it later.
This page is left open for a long time, so an always-running JS animation is a battery cost with no benefit.
Do not invent numbers. No progress percentages, no utilisation figures - this dashboard's rule is that anything without evidence reads as 확인 불가.
The Gemini roster row goes here rather than in CODEX-GEMINI1 because dashboard.py is in this task's allowlist and not in that one's. Do not edit gemini_client.py from here.

Reports/dashboard.html is a TRACKED file and is in your allowlist for exactly this reason: you should regenerate it to check your work, and without it listed that correct action would have been reported as going outside the allowlist.

tasks.title: ParallaxBackground so the level can have background art
tasks.goal: The level has no background art at all - just a generated sky gradient. The approved kenney-background-elements-remastered pack cannot be used because nothing scrolls a background layer yet. Add that component so the art becomes a file copy afterwards.
acceptance: One MonoBehaviour that scrolls N background layers horizontally at per-layer speed factors, so distant layers move slower than near ones.
Structural wiring goes in a SetReferences/SetLayers method called at edit time; numeric tuning goes in a Configure method called at runtime. That split is a project rule, see CLAUDE.md.
Layers repeat seamlessly: when a layer has scrolled one full sprite width it wraps, with no visible gap or jump.
No allocation per frame - no GetComponent, no Find, no new objects in Update.
It works with NO layers assigned (does nothing, logs nothing) so a generated scene without background art is unaffected.
Runtime script: it must NOT reference UnityEditor in any form, or the Android build breaks.
Uses current Unity APIs only - Rigidbody2D.linearVelocity rather than the obsolete .velocity, if velocity is touched at all.
notes: Do NOT wire this into SceneGenerator and do NOT copy any art in this task. Those are separate steps that need the art files present first, and SceneGenerator.cs is not in your allowlist.
Read Assets/GameFactory/Gameplay/Runner/GroundSpawner.cs first - it already solves the recycle-when-passed problem for ground tiles and the same idiom should be used here rather than a new one.
The camera is orthographic with orthographicSize 5 and follows the player on X only (CameraFollow2D).

tasks.title: Three bugs in the board runner, found by running it for real
tasks.goal: The first real `team run` reported CODEX-ART1 as BLOCKED even though Codex had done the work correctly. Three separate defects in teamwork.py caused or contributed to that, all of them mine. Fix all three.
acceptance: (1) TOOL CHURN MUST NOT BLOCK A TASK. Packages/packages-lock.json is tracked, is not gitignored, and Unity rewrites it whenever the editor re-resolves packages. It changed during the run, so it landed in `after - before`, matched no allowlist, and blocked the task. Add a module-level tuple of paths that are regenerated by tools rather than authored by an agent - Packages/packages-lock.json at minimum - and exclude them from the outside-allowlist check. Report them separately in TaskRun instead of dropping them silently, so a real change there is still visible.

(2) save() MUST NOT CLOBBER HAND-EDITED FIELDS. It hardcodes _comment and _version into the payload on every write, so a comment edited by hand in the JSON is silently reverted the first time run_task saves. Preserve unknown top-level keys and any existing _comment; only write the default when the file had none. A board that cannot be annotated by hand is not the shared, human-readable handoff it is supposed to be.

(3) The concurrent-work warning in build_prompt should track the tree, not the status field. It currently names every in_progress/review task as 'being edited right now', which for already-committed work is false and warns Codex off stable files. List a task only when at least one of its declared files is actually dirty, and name those files. Reuse the existing changed_paths() helper and Task.covers() rather than adding new matching logic.
build_prompt keeps working when git is unavailable or the path is not a repo: fall back to the status-based behaviour rather than raising. A prompt builder must not be able to fail the run.

Tests for each: a tool-churn path does not block a task while a real stray file still does; a hand-edited _comment survives a save/load round trip; a committed REVIEW task is omitted from the warning while a dirty one is included with its filenames; and the no-git fallback.
Existing tests in test_teamwork.py still pass - test_the_prompt_warns_about_concurrent_work may need its fixture to dirty a file rather than only set a status.
notes: Read teamwork.py fully first. changed_paths() already handles renames and untracked files, and Task.covers() already matches a path against a task's allowlist patterns.
Keep it cheap: build_prompt runs once per run, so one git call is fine, but do not call git once per task.

Do NOT gitignore Packages/packages-lock.json to make the symptom go away. Unity projects are supposed to commit it so package versions stay pinned; the fix is that the allowlist check should know the difference between a tool regenerating a file and an agent editing one.

A SPEC-WRITING RULE worth keeping, recorded here because _comment gets overwritten until defect (2) is fixed: when a task edits a GENERATOR, the generator's committed OUTPUT belongs in that task's allowlist too, or verifying the change reads as going out of bounds. That is why Reports/dashboard.html is listed on CODEX-OFFICE1.
